name: Frame-by-Frame Animation
visualIdentity: Individually drawn frames with consistent character proportions, intentional line variation, planned key drawings, in-betweens, and exposure holds. At 24 fps, animation on twos uses 12 drawings per second; output frame rate is not drawing rate. The style is a supplemental reference, not a confirmed source-collection style.
suitableUses: Explicit fit: character performance shots, illustrated mascots, anime, cartoon, storybook, rigged characters, and expressive product or explainer scenes. Hybrids suit poetic shorts or picture-book narratives with static watercolor plates, or dialogue and reaction holds with prepared line-boil variants. Chaptered or scroll-driven storytelling is suitable only when it supports a meaningful narrative. These are suitability judgments, not intrinsic requirements.
limitations: Moving one image or adding random jitter does not create frame-by-frame drawing. Frames must be independently drawn or redrawn at planned exposure intervals. Preserve silhouette, proportions, cadence, and holds; do not add automatic smoothing or interpolated poses. Eye-following needs readable eyes and suitable layers or a rig; omit it if it distorts anatomy or distracts. Chapter transitions need meaningful boundaries and must not obscure causality or violate a continuous-shot requirement.
palette: No intrinsic palette is specified. The optional four-color example assigns background #F5EEDC, foreground #303C44, accent_1 #72929A, and accent_2 #BF7C65; these are suggestions only. Task, brand, approved reference, existing semantic colors, and artwork take precedence. Keep colors discrete; gradients are disabled. Suggested accent-on-foreground pairs fail the normal-text contrast target, so use the main background for body text and check actual composited frames. Do not recolor assets or add hues for contrast.
motionAndInteraction: Keep planned exposure cadence and held states; derive poses from seekable composition time. Line boil may cycle 2–3 aligned variants only during holds, at a consistent cadence; never use random per-frame jitter or boil action drawings. Interactive HTML may use pointer gaze or finite scroll progress for chapters and story states, with coherent reverse and direct seeking, readable holds, keyboard/touch support where appropriate, and reduced-motion behavior. Video must use authored target paths and composition time, never live input. Motion references are optional and require scene support.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or required layer is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Synchronize picture and sound on shared timing, preserve speech clarity, avoid clipping, and inspect the final mix.
assetRequirements: Prepare transparent, consistently sized, clearly named numbered frames or layered artwork with a manifest. Maintain character model proportions and intentional linework. Watercolor hybrids require static plates; line-boil requires 2–3 aligned variants; gaze interaction needs eye layers or a suitable rig. Inspect assets before composition.
combinations: Works alone for character performance. Static watercolor backgrounds can contrast with drawn characters if their hues fit the reference palette, plates remain still, and textures do not muddy silhouettes. Prepared line-boil variants suit holds only. Use story, chapter, or gaze patterns only when the scene supports their geometry and purpose; none is mandatory.
productionApproach: Choose the style renderer and motion engine for fidelity and action; Canvas 2D is the direct drawing option, with PixiJS or p5.js optional for deterministic layered or procedural rendering. Rough.js can prepare seeded sketch contours but cannot supply poses, handwriting, or authentic drawing media. Use one owner per animated property and cache or deterministically replay state. HyperFrames is the primary composition, timing, synchronization, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. Keep rendering and motion logic in their own layers; inspect opening, action, transition, closing, backward-seek, audio-sync, and loop states.
